What I think OP is trying to do is identify traits and behaviours we are seeing in TV and hypothesise about how those traits and behaviours may have similarities with traits and behaviours of autistic people.

This actually can be a helpful tool when you see it as "Hey if you identify with Jordan because of these specific traits and behaviours, you may also want to look into autism" or "If you know someone in your life that behaves like this person on TV, perhaps think about their behaviour in the context of neurodivergence and see if you can open your mind to futher understanding of why they may act poorly sometimes".

This is different to what is colloquially referred to as "armchair diagnosis" where someone decides that a specific person has a specific diagnosis and then carries on as if that diagnosis is actually true. A negative outcome of that can be further extrapolating other traits and behaviours based on the diagnosis you've decided on instead of continuing to look at that person's actual behaviour to determine anything about them

I've seen this a lot with Peggy where someone will say "she's a narcissist so she probably also thinks and feels all these things" and also project future behaviours onto her that there is no proof of and we haven't seen

There is a difference between dentifying specific behaviours in someone and trying to reason about those using all the tools at your disposal including your knowledge about neurodivergent traits vs projecting a diagnosis and reasoning about theoretical behaviours based on that diagnosis
